blocks.prompt: 11 A mechanic applies a force of 50 pounds along the positive x-axis on a wrench connected to a bolt. The pivot point of the wrench is at the origin \((0, 0, 0)\), and the force is applied at the point \((0 \text{ ft}, 2 \text{ ft}, 3 \text{ ft})\). Determine the torque produced by this force about the pivot point.
blocks.explanation:
A real-life cross product question: torque (turning effect) \(\underline{\tau} = \underline{r} \times \underline{F}\).
We must find the torque vector about the origin.
Plan: write \(\underline{F}\) and \(\underline{r}\) as vectors, then take the determinant for \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\).
steps:
Given: force 50 lb along the positive \(x\)-axis; pivot \(O(0, 0, 0)\); point of application \(P(0, 2, 3)\) ft.
To find: the torque \(\underline{\tau}\) about \(O\).
Method: \(\underline{\tau} = \underline{r} \times \underline{F}\), where \(\underline{r} = \overrightarrow{OP}\) runs from the pivot to the point where the force acts (Key Concept, 14.4.6).

Write the vectors
\[\underline{F} = 50\underline{i} + 0\underline{j} + 0\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{r} = \overrightarrow{OP} = 0\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
Why: "50 pounds along the positive \(x\)-axis" is 50 in the \(\underline{i}\) direction only. The pivot is the origin, so \(\underline{r}\) is just the coordinates of \(P\).

Cross product
\[\underline{\tau} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 50 & 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (0 - 0)\underline{i} - (0 - 150)\underline{j} + (0 - 100)\underline{k}\]
\[= 150\underline{j} - 100\underline{k}\]
Why: Minors \((2)(0) - (3)(0) = 0\), \((0)(0) - (3)(50) = -150\) (with sign \(-\) gives \(+150\)), \((0)(0) - (2)(50) = -100\). The order is \(\underline{r}\) first, then \(\underline{F}\).

Size and check
\[|\underline{\tau}| = \sqrt{150^2 + 100^2} = 50\sqrt{13}\]
\[\approx 180.3 \text{ lb-ft}\]
\[\underline{\tau} \cdot \underline{F} = 0,\quad \underline{\tau} \cdot \underline{r} = 300 - 300 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Torque must be perpendicular to both \(\underline{r}\) and \(\underline{F}\), and it is. The units are pound \(\times\) foot.
